01.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Separate AC and DC charger requirements by output power, connector standard, enclosure rating, communications protocol and destination-market certification.
Freeze commercial assumptions for sample quantity, pilot quantity, production MOQ, branding, spare parts and warranty response before comparing quotations.
Require a common compliance-document list so certificates, test reports and model coverage can be compared on the same basis.
screening: Confirm the supplier is the manufacturer or clearly identify any trading-company role and the actual production entity.
Compare charger platform ownership, firmware and OCPP support, connector sourcing, enclosure production, test capability and after-sales structure.
Reject quotations that cannot map the quoted model to the requested power, interface, certification and warranty scope.
validation: Review datasheets, certification scope, electrical protection, thermal management, connector configuration, communication behavior and sample configuration before pilot approval.
Record sample deviations against one controlled requirement matrix instead of accepting changes through chat history.
Define pre-shipment checks for labeling, serial traceability, accessories, firmware/version evidence, packaging and required documents.
handover: Approved requirement matrix and model-selection record.
Supplier comparison, compliance-document register and sample approval record.
Production release checklist, inspection plan, packing requirements and spare-parts list.

07.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Translate drawings into a CTQ list covering material grade, heat treatment, critical dimensions, geometric tolerances, surface finish and cosmetic requirements.
Define which dimensions require CMM evidence, which can be checked with gauges and which are fit or assembly characteristics.
Separate prototype pricing from repeat-production pricing and state how fixture, programming and inspection costs are treated.
screening: Compare machine envelope, spindle and axis capability, material experience, fixture design, CMM access and inspection-document discipline.
Check whether special processes such as anodizing, plating, passivation or heat treatment are controlled in-house or subcontracted.
Require sample inspection records that reference the same drawing revision as the quotation.
validation: Use first-article inspection to close dimensional, material and finish requirements before repeat orders.
For critical features, retain measurement evidence and identify the measurement method rather than recording pass/fail only.
Freeze drawing revision, approved deviation list and packaging method before production release.
handover: Controlled drawing and CTQ register.
First-article dimensional report and material/process evidence.
Approved deviation list, packaging standard and repeat-order inspection plan.

13.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Break the BOS package into electrical protection, cables/connectors, enclosures, mounting hardware and project documentation instead of requesting one undifferentiated quote.
State electrical ratings, environmental conditions, applicable standards, project quantities and required document language for each product family.
Define substitution rules so suppliers cannot silently change brands, materials or ratings during execution.
screening: Compare technical ownership, certificate coverage, project references, production lead time and ability to consolidate multiple BOS categories.
Check consistency between datasheets, certificates and quoted model numbers.
Identify which components are manufactured by the supplier and which are sourced from approved upstream brands.
validation: Review electrical ratings, material and environmental specifications against the project BOM before sample or batch release.
Use document gates for certificates, declarations, drawings, labels and packing lists before shipment.
For substituted components, require buyer approval before procurement or production.
handover: Approved BOS cross-reference matrix and model list.
Certificate/document register and substitution log.
Consolidation plan, packing list structure and shipment-release checklist.

16.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Define duty point, flow, head, fluid, temperature, material compatibility, seal arrangement, motor efficiency, voltage/frequency and connection requirements.
Separate hydraulic performance requirements from motor, seal, coating, baseplate and accessory requirements.
State required test evidence and spare-parts expectations with the RFQ.
screening: Compare pump-curve capability, casting and machining control, balancing, hydrostatic or performance-test capability, motor sourcing and seal options.
Check whether quoted pump curves and motor selections correspond to the requested duty point rather than a generic catalog range.
Review material certificates, test formats and parts traceability for project-critical applications.
validation: Verify selected operating point, motor margin, materials, seals, coatings and connection dimensions before approval.
Define production inspection for nameplate data, rotation, leakage, vibration/noise where applicable, accessories and packaging.
Freeze spare-parts BOM and documentation requirements before shipment.
handover: Approved pump-selection sheet and performance basis.
Material, motor and seal configuration record.
Inspection/test requirements, spare-parts list and shipment documents.

18.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Control vessel material grade, wall thickness, dimensions, nozzle orientation, weld quality, internal finish, drainability and support geometry from an approved drawing.
Define sanitary finish, passivation, pressure or leak-test requirements and required material/weld documentation where applicable.
Separate transport-frame and export-packing requirements from the fabrication drawing.
screening: Assess stainless fabrication capability, welding qualifications, polishing/finishing capability, dimensional control and inspection documentation.
Review previous vessel work of comparable size and finish without treating unrelated pressure-vessel experience as sufficient evidence.
Identify subcontracted polishing, passivation or testing processes and how they are controlled.
validation: Use drawing approval before cutting and fabrication, with nozzle and interface dimensions treated as CTQs.
Capture weld, finish, dimensional and leak/pressure-test evidence as required by the project.
Approve protection of finished surfaces, openings and transport supports before packing.
handover: Approved fabrication drawing and nozzle schedule.
Material and inspection/test record package appropriate to the project.
Surface-protection, packing and transport-release checklist.

19.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Define pallet dimensions, load per level, bay geometry, clear heights, aisle assumptions, floor/interface constraints and protection requirements from the warehouse layout.
Separate structural rack requirements from decking, guards, anchors, signage and installation sequencing.
Freeze phased delivery requirements so packs arrive in an installation-ready sequence.
screening: Compare upright and beam section capability, steel grade, roll-forming and welding controls, coating process and engineering documentation.
Check that quoted configurations are tied to defined loads and geometry rather than generic rack families.
Review packaging and part-identification methods because missing or mixed hardware creates installation risk even when steelwork is correct.
validation: Approve layout, elevations, member schedule, hardware and load signage before production.
Use dimensional, coating, weld and component-count checks appropriate to the rack system.
Verify pack labels and phased loading plan against the installation sequence.
handover: Approved warehouse layout, elevations and member schedule.
Component packing list and hardware schedule.
Inspection record, phased shipment plan and installation-document package.

21.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Translate room drawings into cabinet module dimensions, material specifications, finish codes, hardware schedule, countertop interfaces and installation tolerances.
Control exposed finish, edge treatment and hardware brand/model separately from cabinet carcass construction.
Define room or unit labeling so mixed-project shipments remain installation-ready.
screening: Compare panel processing, edge banding, drilling, finishing, hardware integration and drawing/BOM control capability.
Review sample door and carcass workmanship under the actual finish specification rather than accepting catalog images.
Assess packing and module-identification methods for export damage and site sorting risk.
validation: Approve shop drawings, finish sample, hardware schedule and critical module dimensions before batch production.
Use packing mock-up or defined corner/edge protection for vulnerable finished panels.
Control room/module labels and packing lists so installation teams can identify complete sets.
handover: Approved shop drawings, finish codes and hardware schedule.
Sample approval and packaging specification.
Room/module packing list and installation handover documentation.

25.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Freeze resin grade, color, texture, critical dimensions, cosmetic zones, inserts, assembly interfaces and annual-volume assumptions before tooling quotation.
Separate mold ownership, cavity count, mold life, maintenance, change costs and sample stages from piece-price comparison.
Define which appearance defects are unacceptable in A-surfaces and which dimensions are CTQs.
screening: Compare mold design capability, injection-machine range, resin experience, toolroom ownership, measurement equipment and cosmetic-part discipline.
Review how the supplier controls resin, masterbatch, regrind, drying, process parameters and mold maintenance.
Require tooling and production quotations to reference the same drawing and volume assumptions.
validation: Use structured sample stages to close fit, dimensions, appearance, texture, color and process stability before mass-production release.
Maintain an approved sample and controlled defect standard for cosmetic surfaces.
Record approved process/material changes rather than allowing substitutions after sample sign-off.
handover: Approved drawing, resin/color specification and cosmetic standard.
Tooling scope/ownership record and approved sample status.
Mass-production control plan, packaging specification and change-control record.

31.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Define connector manufacturer/part number, wire gauge and insulation, pinout, length tolerances, labels, terminals, overmold or sleeving and electrical-test requirements.
Control approved component substitutions because connector and terminal look-alikes can create fit, plating and reliability risk.
State pull-force, continuity, polarity and any insulation or high-voltage test criteria applicable to the harness.
screening: Compare crimping equipment, applicator control, terminal sourcing, wire processing, test fixtures, traceability and operator inspection methods.
Check whether key connectors and terminals are authentic specified components or locally substituted equivalents.
Review crimp-quality evidence and how tooling wear or applicator changes are controlled.
validation: Approve first samples for pinout, length, labels, connector fit, crimp appearance and electrical continuity.
For critical terminals, use pull-force or crimp-section evidence as defined by the project.
Lock BOM and approved substitution list before production.
handover: Controlled harness drawing, pinout and BOM.
Approved sample and electrical/mechanical test requirements.
Production test record format, label/traceability rule and packing specification.

35.label: Hero control plan
requirements: Break the FF&E package into room linen, amenities, tabletop, small appliances and room accessories with an approved room or SKU schedule.
Define brand, finish, size, packaging and replacement-stock requirements for visually coordinated items.
Control consolidation deadlines by hotel opening or refurbishment sequence rather than treating each supplier independently.
screening: Compare suppliers by product-specific capability, consistency, hospitality packaging, export readiness and replenishment ability instead of forcing one supplier to cover every category.
Check sample appearance, material and finish consistency across items that must coordinate in the same guest room.
Evaluate carton labeling and consolidation discipline for room-based or department-based receiving.
validation: Approve representative samples and finish references before purchase release.
Use SKU, room, quantity and packaging checks during consolidation to prevent incomplete room sets.
Confirm spare/replacement quantities and final packing lists before shipment.
handover: Approved FF&E/SKU schedule and sample references.
Supplier-by-category allocation and consolidation tracker.
Room/department packing list, replacement-stock record and shipment-release checklist.
